From residential homes to commercial properties and fleet operations, properly installed EV charging stations are essential infrastructure for a sustainable future. The Explosive Growth of EV Charging Infrastructure in 2025

The numbers tell a compelling story about the rapid expansion of EV charging infrastructure in America. The United States has experienced unprecedented growth in recent years, with public EV charging ports reaching nearly 196,000 ports by 2025, up from approximately 30,000 just a decade ago. This represents a staggering 6-fold increase, demonstrating the nation's commitment to EV infrastructure development.

In 2025 alone, America is on track to add approximately 16,700 new fast-charging ports, representing a nearly 20 percent year-over-year increase. The deployment of ultra-fast chargers has accelerated significantly, with 63 percent of new ports featuring 250+ kilowatt power levels, compared to just 25 percent two years ago. This shift toward higher-power infrastructure means faster charging times and better customer experiences for EV drivers.

Los Angeles plays a crucial role in this national expansion. California now has 48 percent more EV chargers than gasoline nozzles throughout the state, and Los Angeles continues to lead West Coast cities in charging infrastructure development. The City of Los Angeles recently announced the deployment of 90 new curbside Level-2 charging ports across the city over the next 12 months, providing more convenient options for residents and businesses. Additionally, Los Angeles County has over 750 public charging stations and has adopted an ambitious Zero-Emission Vehicle Master Plan that calls for approximately 3,700 additional chargers, positioning the region as a national leader in sustainable transportation infrastructure.

Understanding EV Charging Technology and Power Levels

Not all EV chargers are created equal, and understanding the different types of charging technology is essential for making informed decisions about your charging needs. The landscape of EV charging technology continues to evolve, with innovations focused on improving reliability, speed, and accessibility for all users. The right charging solution for you depends on your vehicle type, driving habits, property characteristics, and budget considerations.

Level 1 chargers operate on standard 120-volt household outlets and deliver approximately 2-3 miles of range per hour of charging, making them suitable only for overnight residential charging or occasional supplemental charging. They are the slowest charging option but require no electrical upgrades. Level 2 chargers require a dedicated 240-volt circuit and provide 10-30 miles of range per hour, making them the standard choice for most residential installations and commercial applications. Level 2 chargers offer an excellent balance between charging speed and installation cost, and they work well for daily EV charging scenarios. DC fast chargers, the most advanced option, can deliver 200+ miles of range in just 30 minutes, though they require specialized electrical infrastructure and are typically deployed along highways and in commercial fleet operations.

The increasing prevalence of 350+ kilowatt ultra-fast chargers reflects the industry's push toward reducing charging times and improving driver convenience. These high-powered installations enable cross-country EV travel and commercial fleet charging operations. For residential and small commercial applications in Los Angeles, Shaffer Construction typically recommends Level 2 hardwired installations, which provide reliable, efficient charging without the infrastructure demands of DC fast chargers. Our team conducts thorough site assessments to determine the best charging solution for your specific property and electrical capacity, considering factors like your typical daily driving distance, vehicle battery size, and available budget.

According to industry best practices for EV charger installation, hardwired Level 2 chargers are superior to plug-in configurations because they provide better durability, improved security, and resistance to wear and tear. Hardwired installations eliminate the risk of charging cables being unplugged accidentally, provide faster charging compared to plug-in models, and integrate more seamlessly with home and business electrical systems. A Level 2 charger operating at 40 amps requires a dedicated 50-amp electrical circuit, calculated using the continuous load rating of 125 percent, as specified in electrical codes. This proper sizing ensures safe, reliable operation and protects your home or business from electrical hazards and potential fire risks.

Essential Electrical Requirements and Installation Best Practices

Installing an EV charger is not a simple DIY project. It requires careful electrical planning, professional expertise, and strict adherence to local and national electrical codes. At Shaffer Construction, Inc., our licensed electricians follow industry best practices to ensure every installation is safe, compliant, and built to last.

The first critical step is a comprehensive electrical panel assessment. Many properties in Los Angeles have older electrical systems that may not have sufficient capacity for a Level 2 EV charger. Our electricians evaluate your current panel amperage, existing loads, and future expansion potential to determine if an upgrade is necessary. Inadequate panel capacity is one of the most common obstacles to EV charger installation, and addressing this issue upfront prevents costly problems later.

All EV charging equipment must include ground fault circuit interrupter (GFCI) protection, a critical safety feature that cuts power instantly if a ground fault is detected, preventing dangerous electrical shocks. Additionally, proper wiring and grounding are essential throughout the installation. Our team uses industry-approved materials and installation techniques that comply with the National Electrical Code and local Los Angeles building standards.

Permits and inspections are not optional steps that can be skipped to save time and money. Los Angeles requires permits for EV charger installations, and our team handles all paperwork and coordinates with city inspectors to ensure your installation meets all regulatory requirements. This protects your investment and ensures that your charging equipment is safe and properly integrated with your home or business electrical system.

As we detailed in our comprehensive guide to EV charging infrastructure for Los Angeles property owners, proper electrical planning and professional installation are the foundation of reliable EV charging infrastructure.

EV Charging Solutions for Residential and Commercial Properties

The benefits of installing EV chargers extend far beyond the convenience of charging at home or work. For residential properties, EV chargers increase home value, provide energy independence, and enable owners to take advantage of off-peak electricity rates through smart charging features. Homeowners can schedule charging during hours when electricity costs are lowest, potentially reducing monthly energy expenses.

For commercial properties, installing EV chargers provides competitive advantages in attracting tenants, customers, and employees who drive electric vehicles. Businesses and property developers recognize that comprehensive charging infrastructure is increasingly expected by consumers and employees alike. Retail centers, office parks, multifamily residential buildings, and hospitality properties that lack EV charging are at a disadvantage in the competitive real estate market.

Fleet operators and property managers benefit significantly from EV charger installations by reducing fuel costs, lowering maintenance expenses, and demonstrating corporate environmental responsibility. Companies throughout Los Angeles are upgrading their facilities to support their transition to electric fleet vehicles, and Shaffer Construction provides the commercial EV charger installation expertise needed to make these transitions seamless.

However, commercial installations introduce additional complexity. Multi-unit properties, parking structures, and fleet operations often require load management systems to prevent electrical overloads, careful planning to minimize installation costs, and strategic placement of chargers to maximize accessibility and utilization. Each commercial property presents unique challenges that require professional expertise to address effectively.

Many property owners underestimate the importance of electrical load studies before installing multiple EV chargers. Our team can conduct thorough electrical load studies to assess your facility's capacity and recommend cost-effective solutions for supporting your charging infrastructure goals.

Planning Your EV Charging Project: A Roadmap for Success

Successfully installing EV charging infrastructure requires careful planning, realistic budgeting, and partnership with experienced professionals. Property owners in Los Angeles should approach EV charger installation as a strategic investment in their property's future value and functionality.

Begin by assessing your charging needs. Residential customers should evaluate their current vehicle, driving patterns, and future plans. A homeowner who commutes 30 miles daily and has regular access to Level 2 charging may only need 120-volt charging, while someone with longer commutes benefits from a dedicated 240-volt Level 2 charger. Commercial property managers must evaluate tenant or employee needs, parking capacity, and expected utilization to determine the appropriate number of chargers and their placement.

Next, conduct a professional site assessment. This is where experienced electricians like those at Shaffer Construction evaluate electrical panel capacity, determine if upgrades are necessary, assess property layout for optimal charger placement, and identify any challenges or obstacles. This assessment provides the foundation for accurate budgeting and successful project execution.

Budgeting should account for the charger equipment itself, electrical upgrades or panel replacement if needed, installation labor, permitting and inspection fees, and any structural modifications required for outdoor installations. While initial costs can be significant, multiple incentive programs can offset expenses. Federal tax credits, California state rebates, utility company incentives, and local Los Angeles programs may be available depending on your property type and location.

Our detailed article on planning EV charger infrastructure in Los Angeles covers costs, options, and what to expect throughout the installation process, providing valuable information to help guide your decision-making.

Every installation contributes to this network and helps accelerate the adoption of clean transportation throughout Los Angeles and California.
